chunks.text:
elongation and termination.

Although the enzymatic process of elongation is essentially the same in eukaryotes and prokaryotes, the DNA
template is considerably more complex. When eukaryotic cells are not dividing, their genes exist as a diffuse mass
of DNA and proteins called chromatin. The DNA is tightly packaged around charged histone proteins at repeated
intervals. These DNA–histone complexes, collectively called nucleosomes, are regularly spaced and include 146
nucleotides of DNA wound around eight histones like thread around a spool. For polynucleotide synthesis to occur, the transcription machinery needs to move histones out of the way every time
it encounters a nucleosome.

result.question: What does fixation mean in biology?
result.answer: In the context of the Calvin cycle, fixation refers to the first stage where carbon dioxide (CO2) is incorporated into an organic molecule, specifically ribulose bisphosphate (RuBP), catalyzed by the enzyme RuBisCO.
